Cook visited Apple's Battersea campus in London this week to meet King Charles, as part of a new collaboration between the company and The King's Trust.

At Apple's Battersea headquarters, Cook also sat down for an in-depth interview with The Independent, discussing the collaboration and his thoughts after the first month as Apple's executive chairman.

Cook stepped down as Apple CEO last month, handing the role over to John Ternus. In this week's interview, Cook revealed that the handover "actually began a few years ago."

Ternus took over as CEO right around the launch of the iPhone Duo, which Cook said was fully mapped out under his tenure. Cook explained: "I wanted to give John a tailwind right from the start, and Apple's tailwind is, to a large extent, built on the product cycle."

Cook also stressed that, as Apple's executive chairman, he now focuses on "global policy" matters, and noted that he and Ternus share "an exceptionally high degree of trust." Cook is helping Ternus "in whatever way he sees fit," but he made it clear that he "will not interfere."

What advice did Cook give Ternus? Simply, "don't try to be me." The full interview is available at The Independent and also includes a fascinating discussion of the new collaboration between Apple and The King's Trust.
